objective: Reduce Hunter V2 shadow evidence cost without weakening rollout policy or the certified six-item recommendation contract.

attempts.controlIssue: One V1 control observation returned zero measured cost and an unusually short no-op-like latency, making relative cost/latency aggregation non-comparable.
All three Python V1 control observations returned zero measured cost with 210-459ms latency while V2 completed full evidence work, confirming a repeatable non-comparable control baseline.

verifiedFindings: V2 paid search cost decreased from $0.021 to $0.014 per comparison (33.3% reduction).
All 18 V2 comparisons across the two pre-gate attempts retained 100% retrieval coverage and 0% V2 failures.
Every V2 comparison retained six selected recommendations with exactly one exploration recommendation (16.7%) and maximum topic share of 16.7%.
The 30-pair gate was not run because relative cost and latency thresholds cannot be evaluated reliably against zero/no-op V1 control observations.
nextGate: Restore explicit control comparability without changing the 1.5x cost/latency limits, then rerun 3x3 before any 30-pair gate.
